# `check_ai_process`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Check a mosaic image for black gaps before AI processing.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit and 32-bit builds) |
| Side-effect tier | B |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xdb180, CheckMosaicGap @0x3f1c80 (64-bit build) |

Reads (or relays to the peer process by the same routing as start_ai_process) and tests the current or named image for black gaps, optionally after rotating and cropping with the first eight crop integers. Neither starts a worker nor saves output. Image-load failure is reported as gap_ok true, not as an error. No event is emitted. Although the app calls it from a mosaic-completion routine, it is not a signal that the device finished all mosaic centers and does not end a mosaic round or plan item (INFERRED). Firmware 9.75, app 3.4.0 replaces the old view-mode test with the relay-only form of the common relay check (it relays to the peer process when needed and runs no occupancy probe, so no 203 or 524 comes from it; READ in 64-bit firmware 9.75), the wire effect is INFERRED and the 32-bit build was not checked.

Side effects: Allocates temporary image buffers; relay and logging bookkeeping only. Nothing is saved and no worker starts.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"check_ai_process"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object | no | - | Object params only; arrays, scalars and null mean no keys (current image, no crop). These are the only keys read; the adjustment, dbe and sharp members of start_ai_process are ignored. [READ] |
| `params.name` | string | no | empty string = current image | Image to process, resolved against the image root. Default empty selects the current image. Non-string (including null) is rejected with 105. [READ] |
| `params.crop` | array<integer> | no | [-1,0,0,0,0,0,0,0] | Crop polygon as up to eight integers. Absent defaults to [-1,0,0,0,0,0,0,0]; only the first eight elements are read, short or empty arrays leave the rest at default, extras are ignored. A negative first value means no crop. INFERRED to be four (x,y) corner pairs in image pixels; no bounds or order validation. Non-integer element is rejected with 104, non-array or null with 102. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (error) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 105 | name present but not a string | `expected string param` |
| 102 | crop present but not an array | `invalid params` |
| 104 | A crop element among the first eight is not an integer | `expected int param` |
| 300 | Relay: main-process user context is null | `internal error` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Transport error codes on relay failure are unresolved.

## Example

Request, current - Default check (invented):

```json
{"id":51,"method":"check_ai_process","params":{}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"check_ai_process","result":{"gap_ok":true},"code":0,"id":51}
```

Reply, error:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"check_ai_process","error":"expected string param","code":105,"id":52}
```
